To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two crystal structures of a 16 kDa galactose-specific plant lectin from Articarpus hirsute have been solved and refined to 2.5 and 3.0 A resolution.
the crystal structure of a lectin from Articarpus hirsutus has been solved at two different resolutions.

(1) The crystal structures of the Artocarpus lectin in complex with methyl-α-D-galactose were solved at two different resolutions, 2.5 and 3.0 A, and (2) The structures reveal that the lectin is composed of two domains and the ligand is bound to the C-terminal domain in an extended conformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure of the galactose-specific Artocarpus lectin and its complexes with the monosaccharide galactose and its analogues.
the synthesis of novel, highly selective, fluorescent chemosensors and the application of these chemosensors for the detection of various metal ions and anions in solution and in the solid state.
the synthesis, characterization, and application of a novel class of polymeric compounds, which have the ability to selectively bind to a specific biological target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the galactose-specific A. hirsuta lectin is similar to that of other galactose-specific plant lectins and is a member of the legume lectin family.
the two structures reported in this work are in agreement and are consistent with the results of previous studies.
